SMTO-GWT-0011 — The Gateway refused a request that changed on the way

GUID: d7145ed9-e992-443f-8d01-fcc5c2d97d7c
Slug: gateway-body-digest-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway checks that every request arrives exactly as SMTO sent it. This one didn't match, so the Gateway refused it and did nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If a proxy, VPN or security filter sits between SMTO and that computer, ask whoever manages the network to let SMTO's traffic to the Gateway pass unchanged. Tools that inspect or rewrite web traffic can alter a request after SMTO signs it.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand the Gateway's row, and select Check for updates. Install any offered update once nothing is running there. Matching versions make sure both sides check requests the same way.
  3. Run the task again. SMTO builds and signs a brand-new request each time, and the refused one never ran.

What success looks like

  • The task runs on that computer without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and the network. Don't install Gateway files by hand to force a version; use the update buttons in Settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's authentication middleware hashed the received request body and it did not match the body digest covered by the Server's signature, so the request was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • The Gateway hashed the received request body and found that it differed from the digest protected by the controller's signature. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway hashed the received request body and found that it differed from the digest protected by the controller's signature.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare protocol versions and retained integrity failure details; investigate body rewriting or incorrect signing without logging secrets.

How to fix it

  • The x-smto-body-sha256 digest signed by the Server differed from the SHA-256 of the body the Gateway received. Look for an intermediary that rewrites request bodies (TLS-inspecting proxy, compression or encoding middleware) and for Server/Gateway version skew; upgrade through the supported update path and let the Server sign a fresh request rather than resending the old body and signature.
  • Inspect protocol compatibility and generate a fresh authenticated request. Do not reuse a corrupted body or signature.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly constructed authorized request passes the body-digest check before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
